answer: Endorsement-Provenance Mirror Audit 1) An identity, the pearl, registers and shares a unique cryptographic delta. 2) A second identity, acting as a prism, endorses the pearl, linking their delta. 3) Auditors verify this link by independently computing the delta of the pearl and checking against the prism's recorded endorsement. Cost for N identities is $5 x N$. The maximum number of endorsements an identity can make is 10. Failure occurs if a sybil controls both the pearl and the prism, creating a false endorsement.
